headline: **MLB Daily Roundup: June 22, 2026**
article:
The Cincinnati Reds secured a 4-1 victory over the New York Yankees, with Chase Burns earning the win after 5.0 innings of work. Tyler Stephenson led the Reds' offense with a home run, 3 RBI, and 1 hit in 4 at-bats. The Milwaukee Brewers also secured a win, taking down the Atlanta Braves 9-4 behind Robert Gasser's 6.0 innings of work with 7 strikeouts.

Several players have been impacted by injuries, with Blas Castaño (Colorado Rockies) being placed on the 15-day injured list due to a right pectoral strain. Other notable injuries include Josh Ekness (Miami Marlins) being transferred to the 60-day injured list with a right calf strain, and Adley Rutschman (Baltimore Orioles) being placed on the 7-day injured list with a concussion.

The Atlanta Braves bolstered their bullpen with the acquisition of right-handed pitcher Tyler Schoff in a trade with the Washington Nationals. The Chicago Cubs also made a trade, acquiring right-hander Jayden Murray from the Houston Astros in exchange for first baseman Cameron Sisneros.

top_news.title: **Nationals Fall Short in Tampa**
top_news.summary: The Washington Nationals dropped a 3-4 decision to the Tampa Bay Rays, unable to overcome a late deficit. Jonny DeLuca led the Nationals' offense with a 2-hit, 1-home run performance, including a key 4th-inning homer that scored Yandy Díaz.

top_news.title: **Tigers Take Down White Sox in Thrilling Finish**
top_news.summary: The Detroit Tigers edged out the Chicago White Sox 5-4 in a closely contested matchup. Dillon Dingler led the Tigers' offense with a 2-hit, 1-home run performance, driving in 2 runs.

top_news.title: **Rockies RHP Blas Castaño Lands on Injured List**
top_news.summary: Colorado Rockies right-hander Blas Castaño has been placed on the 15-day injured list due to a right pectoral strain, effective retroactive to June 18, 2026.

top_news.title: **Braves Bolster Bullpen with Trade Acquisition**
top_news.summary: The Atlanta Braves have acquired right-handed pitcher Tyler Schoff in a trade with the Washington Nationals.
